# Pet voice — lessons

The top block is regenerated by `python3 pet_voice.py learn` from every receipt in
`evidence/`. It also writes `learned/voice-scores.json`, which the next `talk`/`relay`
reads: model order (working, fastest first), the accepted TTS request shape per model and
voice×language intelligibility (`--adapt` swaps a voice that listeners keep mis-hearing).
The curated section below is for lessons a script cannot infer — add one line per new lesson.

## Curated lessons

### Personality (persona lab, `persona_lab.py`)

- **Company copy in → brochure out.** Relay personas built from `pet.json` taglines gave 86 %
  template lines ("statement + Name, how do you X?"), 91 % question endings, no line under
  9 words, no acting. Every pet sounded like the same assistant in another language. (2026-11-15)
- **Character bibles + craft rules beat it blind.** Same writer, same scenes: Claude Haiku as
  blind judge preferred the bible arm 4/4 (both orders) — distinct 7.5 vs 5.3, not-generic
  6.5 vs 3.0, natural 7.3 vs 4.8, want-to-listen 7.8 vs 4.3. Mean line 9–11 words vs 25.
  Evidence: `persona-evidence/pilot-20261115.json`. (2026-11-15)
- **Bibles create new tics.** `[short pause]` landed in 8/10 lines, DeepMind opened with
  "Interesting." every time and Codex reused an anchor verbatim. Next: tag budget, catchphrase
  cooldown per scene, verbatim-anchor rejection, and a critic pass before a line is final.
  Delivery notes came out as stage directions ("gestures wildly") — they must be vocal
  (pace, volume, emotion) to be useful for `speech_metadata.style`. (2026-11-15)
- **Scenes beat relays.** A situation with stakes (03:12, crashed demo, 3 % battery) gives
  the pets something to react to; a ring of introductions only produces interviews. (2026-11-15)
- **Scene engine v2 beat the bible pilot 3/4 blind** (Haiku, both orders): not-generic 6.5 vs
  4.5, want-to-listen 7.5 vs 6.75. The tag budget removed the `[short pause]` template named in
  every v1 loss. Still weak: comebacks that don't follow ("That is a meeting disguised as a
  train") and near-synonym tics ("Fascinating." once "Interesting." was spent).
  `scene-evidence/judge-v1-vs-v2-20261115.json`. (2026-11-15)
- **An ensemble is not a rotation.** The v2 director let Arduino and Atech argue for 7 lines
  while three pets waited. Forcing rotation (no A-B-A, max 2 lines while anyone is silent) gave
  everyone a line (longest duet 2, max share 0.17) but lost 0/2 blind to the duet: one-liners
  nobody answered, each pet doing its own bit. Now an argument may run A-B-A-B, then a third
  voice must take a side, twist it or undercut it, and a pet's first line has to come in on
  the line before it. Not yet tested live (text quota ran out) — run `v2d` and judge it
  against `robot-dog-stage-text-v2`. (2026-11-15)
- **Tell the critic a listed problem is a must-fix.** With "keep" allowed, one critic pass
  left verbatim example lines and question streaks in 6/12 lines of `disk-full-0200` (v2b).
  With "keep is not allowed while a listed problem remains" both v2c scenes ended with 0 open
  problems; the extra critic round for surviving hard problems never had to fire. (2026-11-15)
- **Memory makes running jokes — and new tics.** Rokoko's three-quarter-time waltz carried
  from the crash scene into the ethics scene, MariaDB's 13 May 2018 came back in every
  disk-full run. Good once per scene; so notes now fade (next entry). (2026-11-15)
- **Catch tics by shape, not by list.** Word lists miss the swap ("Fascinating." for a spent
  "Interesting."). The checks now look at shape: a second one-word exclamation opener, a pet
  reheating two content words of its own earlier line, a distinctive three-word lift from an
  example line, and a non-sequitur test (the writer copies what it answers; it must be in the
  last two lines or the beat). Across scenes a habit ledger keeps openers and the content words
  a pet used in two of its last four scenes. Replaying the 9 text receipts, it surfaced exactly
  what the blind judge complained about: Rokoko trekvart/hofterne, NVIDIA thousand/threads,
  MariaDB minns/datum, Atech kettle. Callbacks: one per pet per scene, a note retires after two.
  Live effect not yet measured — every text model was daily-capped by 02:00. (2026-11-15)
- **Voice design works while TTS is capped.** At 02:00, with every TTS model in its daily
  cooldown, `POST /v1beta/voices` still made all 34 voices (~17 s each, 13 s sample each).
  Two descriptions were refused ("Generated voice prompt was flagged by safety policies"):
  AfterQuery's "mischievous edge … barely holding back a laugh" and Cala's "charming,
  conspiratorial". Plain wording ("playful, close to laughing", "friendly, lightly teasing")
  passed first time. The free tier gives each TTS model only ~10–15 calls a day, so the
  designed voice's own model goes first and Live (separate quota) voices fixed transcripts
  for listening tests: 40 lines, fidelity 0.99. (2026-11-15)
- **Fixing the measurable faults did not make better scenes.** With the #228 checks, v2f had 0
  open problems and 0 non-sequiturs, but a blind judge split 3/6 against v2 (mean 32.7 vs
  32.0 of 50; v2 won the crash scene 2/2, v2f lunch 2/2). The owner rated baseline vs v2 audio
  as ties, 2/2. The limit now is story, not tics: nobody answers the lunch question or reacts
  to the admission beat, DeepMind still opens with "Fascinating.", NVIDIA drifts into brochure
  abstraction, and Bahn said Danish "Rytmen" in a German line. Next: beat obligations (the line
  after a beat must react to it), a cross-scene cooldown for signature openers, and a
  language-purity check for Latin-script borrowings. `scene-evidence/judge-v2-vs-v2f-20261115.json`.
  (2026-11-15)
- **Voice design previews are mostly English.** Transcribing six previews: only Bahn (German)
  and Featherless (Japanese) spoke their own language; Rokoko (Danish), Aalto (Finnish) and
  Wendy (Spanish) spoke English. A 👍/👎 on a preview judges timbre, not the language; judge
  language on scene lines. Designed voices work on `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` and
  `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts` only (3.1-flash-tts-preview returned 500, 2.5-flash-preview-tts
  rejects the voice id), and on this free key each of the two stopped after ~8–10 calls on
  15 Nov. So one day buys about 18 designed-voice lines: 8 of the 10 crash-scene lines and 6
  A/B lines got voiced; the rest waits for the next reset. (2026-11-15)
- **On the free key, a designed-voice scene takes two days.** After the 08:00 UTC reset on
  16 Nov, the last crash-scene line (3.8 Flash Lite TTS) and the 3 missing prebuilt A/B lines
  (3.8 Flash TTS) went through first try. `voice-script` resumes per turn, so a scene voiced
  across two days needs no glue. Plan designed-voice work in ~18-line days. (2026-11-16)
- **A voice A/B is only fair on one model.** Both sides of the six A/B pairs use
  `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (`--models` pins it, `speak_line(pinned=True)`), so only the voice
  differs. The page's scene pair (designed voices on 3.8 Flash Lite TTS vs prebuilt voices on
  Live native audio) changes voice and model together, and its setup text says so. (2026-11-16)
- **Designed voices are not equally loud.** In the demo re-cut, the per-line segment level
  ranged ~3x, from Aalto's quiet line to Codex. `demo/build.py` now levels each clip's voiced
  part to one RMS; the listening page still plays raw levels. (2026-11-16)
- **The page db keeps every rating, so ingest must be idempotent.** `db_list` returns the
  15 Nov ties again on every read; running `ingest` twice would have counted them twice.
  `taste.json` now keeps `ingested` (id → rating time) and skips seen ratings; re-ingesting
  the real db left the system counts unchanged. A rating that is changed later counts as a
  new vote. (2026-11-16)
- **The speech code now lives in one shared layer.** Text-to-speech had been built five times in the org, and none of
  the copies shared quota knowledge. The provider code moved unchanged to `SalesSquad/agents` `voice/ssvoice` and
  comes back here as a vendored copy. The shared layer adds a per-machine quota ledger and an audio cache. Live
  check on 16 Nov: a designed-voice Danish line took 3.13 s on gemini-3.8-flash-tts; the identical repeat came from
  the cache, byte-identical, and the ledger counted one call. Tests must point `SSVOICE_HOME` at a temp folder:
  a simulated daily 429 would otherwise cool a real model for hours. (2026-11-16)
- **A paid fallback must stay last by construction.** OpenAI is now the final step for speech
  and text, but the learning loop ranks models by reliability, and OpenAI would soon win and
  become the default spend. `model_order()` therefore always appends `openai:` models after
  every Gemini model, cooling ones included, and a per-process call cap guards the bill. First
  live check: Finnish TTS 2.3 s, transcription fidelity 0.94, writer line clean in 4.0 s. The
  free 3.5 Gemini models stay the writers; OpenAI only fills the hours their daily cap is
  spent. (2026-11-15)
- **Free text quota ≈ 8 scenes a night.** A 12-turn scene costs ~45 Gemini text calls
  (director, writer, critic, memory). After ~8 scenes 3.5-flash-lite and then 3.5-flash hit
  their daily caps (reset ≈ 08:00 UTC). Iterate on text in small batches, judge with Haiku, and
  keep the morning quota for audio. The `gemini-flash-lite-latest` alias answered a probe at
  02:00 but was capped two calls later; 3.6-flash was capped, 3.7-flash 503, 3.8-flash and
  `flash-latest` timed out, the rest 404. It stays as the third writer. (2026-11-15)

- **Use the MBP Keychain key directly in-process.** `gemini-agent` deliberately refuses
  generation (`status|inventory|probe` only); voice work uses `pet_voice.py`, which reads the
  same Keychain item with `/usr/bin/security` and never prints it. (2026-11-14)
- **Check the live model list, not memory.** `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` returned 404 for this
  project although listed; 3.8 TTS/text models worked. `learn` drops 403/404/per-day-quota
  models from the order automatically. (2026-11-14)
- **Newest is not fastest.** On 14 Nov `gemini-3.8-flash` stalled >2 min on an audio+JSON
  listen request while `gemini-3.5-flash` answered in ~8 s (transcript accuracy 0.98) and
  `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` in ~3 s (same accuracy, but it skipped "address the next pet by
  name"). Calls now time out (45 s listen / 90 s TTS) and fall through to the next model;
  `learn` counts timeouts as failures. (2026-11-14)
- **Background jobs over RDC die with the call.** `cmd &` inside `start_process` was killed;
  run long relays in a named tmux session via the RDC `session.py` helper. (2026-11-14)
- **Two speakers max per Gemini TTS request**, so multi-agent talk is synthesized per turn;
  that also keeps every pet's own voice and makes runs resumable per turn. (2026-11-14)
- **Free-tier TTS runs out mid-relay.** The personal key got ~45 TTS calls/day across the four
  TTS models; then every model returned per-day 429 with RetryInfo ≈10.6 h (reset ≈08:00 UTC).
  `learn` stores `cooldownUntil` per model and the next run starts with the Live API voices,
  which have a separate quota. `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest` recited a Finnish line
  word for word (fidelity 1.0); `gemini-3.8-live` spoke but returned no transcript. (2026-11-14)
- **A Live voice may answer the line instead of reading it.** In the second relay
  `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest` replied to two lines in its own words (script
  fidelity 0.19), so the next listener heard something the speaker never "said". Every Live
  turn now checks `outputAudioTranscription` against the script, re-voices once with a
  stricter frame below 0.8, and `learn` multiplies each TTS model's rank by its mean
  fidelity. (2026-11-14)
- **Any provider error should fall through, not stop the relay.** `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`
  returned 503 "high demand" six times in a row and the relay stopped at turn 26 although
  two other listen models were available. Now every non-400 error moves to the next model;
  the run resumes from the failed turn with the same `--run-id`. (2026-11-14)
- **Older TTS models reject `speech_metadata`** (400 on 3.1-preview and 2.5-preview); the
  style-prefix request works. The accepted shape per model is learned, so later calls skip
  the failing attempt. (2026-11-14)
- **Listeners drift into the language they just heard.** In the first full relay a fi-FI pet
  answered in Danish and hi-IN came back in English (language kept 91 %). Fix: the turn prompt
  now repeats the target language and asks for native script. Second relay: language kept
  91 % → 97 %; the same fi-FI pet now answered Danish in Finnish and hi-IN came back in
  Devanagari. (2026-11-14)
- **A listener can "hear" the wrong language.** Meta (en-US) transcribed MariaDB's Swedish as
  garbled English (accuracy 0.58). That pair is listed as weak; with two such samples
  `--adapt` swaps the speaker's voice. (2026-11-14)
- **Score the voice against what was actually said.** When the Live voice paraphrased, the
  first scoring blamed six English voices. Live turns now carry `ttsSpoken`; voice×language
  clarity compares the listener's transcript with that, and script fidelity is a separate
  TTS-model metric. Open limitation: a listener that transliterates (Devanagari ↔ Latin)
  scores near 0 although it understood — hi-IN 0.52 needs a script-aware check. (2026-11-14)
- **Overwriting a file iCloud is syncing can fail.** Re-finalizing a resumed run raised
  EDEADLK ("Resource deadlock avoided") on the iCloud copy and stopped before `learn`.
  Copies now go through a temp file + `os.replace` with retries, and failures are reported in
  the receipt instead of crashing. (2026-11-15)
- **Measure intelligibility, don't guess it.** The listener only receives audio; comparing
  its transcript with what the speaker meant to say gives a free per-voice, per-language
  quality signal on every turn. (2026-11-14)
